title: BIO 201 ( UNIZIK ) : CHEMICAL NATURE OF GENES AND GENE INTERACTIONS
subject: BIO 201

questions.question: The structure of an organism that contains instructions for growth and reproduction is called a what?
questions.explanation: A genome is defined as the structure of an organism that contains instructions for growth and reproduction.

questions.question: Chromosomes are composed primarily of nucleic acid and which other component?
questions.explanation: Chromosomes are physical structures composed primarily of nucleic acid with structural proteins.

questions.question: Which proteins are majorly associated with chromosomes?
questions.explanation: The major proteins associated with chromosomes are the histones.

questions.question: Histones are basic proteins because they are rich in which amino acids?
questions.explanation: Histones are basic because they are rich in lysine and arginine.

questions.question: Due to their amino acid composition, histones are charged in which manner?
questions.explanation: Histones are positively charged because their amino acids have a free amino group that can acquire a proton.

questions.question: DNA is negatively charged because of the presence of which groups?
questions.explanation: DNA is negatively charged because of its many phosphate groups.

questions.question: How many types of histone proteins exist in eukaryotic cells?
questions.explanation: Except for sperm cells, the histone proteins of all eukaryotic cells are of five types.

questions.question: Which of the following is classified as a linker histone?
questions.explanation: H1 is the linker histone which locks DNA in place onto the nucleosome.

questions.question: Which of the following is a core histone?
questions.explanation: Core histones include H2A, H2B, H3, and H4.

questions.question: Cells that are very active in protein synthesis have large what?
questions.explanation: Cells active in protein synthesis have large nucleoli because ribosomes are assembled there.

questions.question: Who first introduced the term chromosome?
questions.explanation: The term chromosome was first introduced by Waldeyer in 1888.

questions.question: Chromosomes are made of which chemical complex?
questions.explanation: Chromosomes occur as separate structures in the nucleus and are made of nucleoprotein.

questions.question: Each longitudinal half of a chromosome is called a what?
questions.explanation: Each longitudinal half of the chromosome is called a chromatid.

questions.question: Which scientist worked out the process of mitosis in 1875?
questions.explanation: Mitosis was first worked out by Strasburger, a German botanist in 1875.

questions.question: Chromosome structure is best studied during which stages?
questions.explanation: The structure of the chromosome may best be studied in its metaphase or anaphase stage.

questions.question: The spindle fibers can originate from which source?
questions.explanation: The spindle can originate from the nuclear sap or out of cytoplasm.

questions.question: When do chromosomes first become visible in a cell?
questions.explanation: Chromosomes first become visible early in cell division when chromatin strands shorten and compact.

questions.question: The two chromatids of a chromosome join at which unique point?
questions.explanation: Chromatids are attached to each other at a unique point called the centromere.

questions.question: Uncoiled genetic material from human chromosomes measures roughly how long?
questions.explanation: If uncoiled, the genetic material in human chromosomes would measure roughly 2 meters in length.

questions.question: The average diameter of the nucleus is about how much?
questions.explanation: The average diameter of the nucleus is about 5 to 10 micrometers.

questions.question: Non-living viruses have chromosomes made of what?
questions.explanation: The non-living viruses have chromosomes consisting of either DNA or RNA.

questions.question: Prokaryotic chromosomes consist entirely of which molecule?
questions.explanation: Among organisms with prokaryotic cells, chromosomes consist entirely of DNA.

questions.question: Eukaryotic chromosomes consist primarily of DNA attached to what?
questions.explanation: The chromosomes of a eukaryotic cell consist primarily of DNA attached to a protein core.

questions.question: Viral genetic material is tightly packed into which structure?
questions.explanation: The genetic material of viruses is very tightly packed into the viral head.

questions.question: The single chromosome of a prokaryotic cell lacks what?
questions.explanation: The single chromosome of a prokaryotic cell is not enclosed within a nuclear membrane.

questions.question: Bacterial DNA is combined with which histone-like protein?
questions.explanation: Bacterial DNA is combined with a histone-like protein called HU.

questions.question: Bacterial chromosomes are composed almost exclusively of what?
questions.explanation: Bacterial chromosomes differ from eukaryotic ones in being composed almost exclusively of DNA.

questions.question: Bacterial chromosomes differ from eukaryotic chromosomes by being what shape?
questions.explanation: Bacterial chromosomes are circular, unlike the linear chromosomes of eukaryotes.

questions.question: The HU protein forms structures similar to which eukaryotic structure?
questions.explanation: There is evidence that HU forms structures similar to nucleosomes with the DNA.

questions.question: Bacteria are classified as which type of organisms?
questions.explanation: Bacteria are prokaryotic organisms with an entirely different type of chromosome.

questions.question: The number of chromosomes in body cells is termed what?
questions.explanation: Body or somatic cells contain a diploid number of chromosomes.

questions.question: The number of chromosomes in reproductive cells is termed what?
questions.explanation: Gametes or reproductive cells contain a haploid number of chromosomes.

questions.question: Human somatic cells contain how many chromosomes?
questions.explanation: In humans, the diploid number of chromosomes in somatic cells is 46.

questions.question: The common fruit fly has how many chromosomes?
questions.explanation: The common fruit fly Drosophila melanogaster has 8 chromosomes.

questions.question: The onion plant has how many chromosomes?
questions.explanation: The onion plant has 16 chromosomes.

questions.question: Chromosome number is normally constant for a particular what?
questions.explanation: The number of chromosomes is normally constant for a particular species of plant or animal.

questions.question: When chromosomes fail to separate properly during division, it is called what?
questions.explanation: Nondisjunction occurs when chromosomes that should move to opposite poles move to the same pole.

questions.question: The presence of three chromosomes of one type is known as what?
questions.explanation: The presence of three chromosomes of one type in an otherwise diploid individual is called trisomy.

questions.question: Organisms with more than two complete sets of chromosomes are called what?
questions.explanation: Cells or organisms with more than two complete sets of chromosomes are said to be polyploid.

questions.question: Which drug disrupts the mitotic spindle to stop mitosis?
questions.explanation: Colchicine disrupts the mitotic spindle and stops mitosis in metaphase.

questions.question: Karyotyping reveals distinctive bands that aid in identifying what?
questions.explanation: Karyotyping reveals distinctive bands that aid in identifying homologs, which have identical banding patterns.

questions.question: Large scale changes in the linkages of genes are caused by what?
questions.explanation: Inversions and translocations remove or add large parts of a chromosome, creating large scale changes in gene linkages.

questions.question: A chromosome part breaking off and attaching to a nonhomologous one is called what?
questions.explanation: A translocation occurs when part of a chromosome breaks off and attaches to a nonhomologous chromosome.

questions.question: A specific translocation causes which syndrome?
questions.explanation: Down syndrome can be caused by a translocation between chromosomes 14 and 21.

questions.question: A chromosome segment that is cut out and reversed is known as what?
questions.explanation: In an inversion, a segment of a chromosome is cut out and reversed.

questions.question: Inversions inhibit which genetic process?
questions.explanation: Inversions inhibit recombination by crossing over.

questions.question: Deletions of genome portions are generally considered what?
questions.explanation: While duplications can be a source of novelty, deletions of portions of the genome are generally deleterious.

questions.question: Duplications of genome portions are a source of what?
questions.explanation: Duplications are a source of evolutionary novelty.

questions.question: Drosophila chromosomes are how many times larger than normal chromosomes?
questions.explanation: Drosophila chromosomes are 200 times larger than normal chromosomes and can be easily studied.

questions.question: Who discovered the first sex-linked trait in Drosophila?
questions.explanation: The first sex-linked trait discovered by Morgan was the white eye colour in Drosophila.
